sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page wala1269 and reference record 663823 (hh:phon:Kilungga:Walak)
sources.note: Alt names Lower Pyramid, Wodo; classification Dani (Bromley 1961: 72; 1966-67: 295). Five descriptive refs: Kilungga 2010 phonology; UNIPA Manokwari theses Togodli 2016 (verbal agreement), Setyaningsih 2014 (causatives), Fuida 2014 (relative clauses), Gombo 2018 (pronominal marking) -- none located online (only citations of Gombo 2018 in a Linguistik Indonesia survey article).

sources.note: Index only: 'Walak (Dani area, IJ highlands; also Wodo) Rule 1977, SH' and 'Wodo d of Grand Valley Dani (Baliem Valley IJ; also Walak) W&H 1981; Wodo Valley d of Dani Voegelins 1965'. Rule 1977 = 'Institutional framework of language study: The Asia Pacific Christian Mission' in Wurm (ed.) 1977: 1341-1347 (mission survey, not a description). No phonology of Walak listed.

sources.citation: Bromley, H. Myron. 1961. The Phonology of Lower Grand Valley Dani: A Comparative Structural Study of Skewed Phonemic Patterns. Verhandelingen KITLV 34. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. xvi+98 pp. (OAPEN hdl 20.500.12657/32232)
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'The pattern of Wodo Dani' (printed pp. 10-11, p. 26) = Walak ('spoken in the Wodo valley and in a limited area around Pyramid Mountain'; corrigenda p. IX: 'Wodo is now spelled Wodlo'; data from Ross Bartel and Bromley's own Pyramid notes): gives only the phoneme inventory (Table III) and glottal-stop distribution -- NO stress statement for Wodo/Walak. The book's only word-stress statement (sec. 3.132, printed p. 49, p. 65) is for Lower Grand Valley Dani (lowe1415): 'The phonological word consists of a syllable or group of syllables with only one primary word stress.
